name: Singapore
title: Holidays in Singapore
intro: Glowing supertrees, a night safari and cheap amazing street food in a spotless city. Here's what Singapore is like with the family and when to go.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 7 to 8 hrs ahead of the UK

facts.label: Plugs
facts.value: Type G · same as the UK

facts_note: Fill in the SG Arrival Card online in the three days before you land. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Singapore is hot and humid all year, with short tropical downpours. February to April and July to August tend to be a little drier. Chinese New Year in January or February brings lanterns and parades.

things.name: Gardens by the Bay
things.blurb: Giant supertrees with a free light show each evening. The domes are ticketed.

things.name: Night Safari
things.blurb: A tram ride through a zoo after dark to see animals when they're awake.

things.name: Singapore Zoo
things.blurb: Open enclosures, orangutans and a big water play area.

things.name: Sentosa
things.blurb: An island of beaches, Universal Studios and cable cars.

things.name: Hawker centres
things.blurb: Food courts with dishes for a few pounds. Lau Pa Sat and Maxwell are good starts.

things.name: Jewel Changi
things.blurb: The world's tallest indoor waterfall, at the airport.

faqs.question: Is Singapore good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's very safe, clean and easy, with world-class zoos and gardens. Plan indoor or water play for the hottest part of the day.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Three to five nights, often as a stopover on the way to Bali, Australia or Malaysia.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit without a visa, but must fill in the SG Arrival Card online before landing. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Is Singapore expensive?
faqs.answer: Hotels and attractions are pricey, but hawker food and public transport are cheap.
